summary: Unexpected duplicate downstream webhook invocations after SDK retry-coalescing on process restart
description:
Issue summary: Customer BrightCart reports duplicate webhook deliveries to their downstream order processor after an in-flight function/tool call is retried and the SDK performs 'retry-coalescing' across a process restart.

Impact: Duplicate downstream side effects (double payments in staging subset) observed for ~3% of long-running tool calls during a rolling deploy that restarts worker processes. This is customer-critical (financial exposure).

Environment: BrightCart uses Redwood Dedicated in us-east, Python SDK (v1.17.1) as primary worker, a TypeScript orchestrator microservice that batches requests, and a Go webhook consumer behind an edge proxy.

Observed behavior: On process restart mid-stream the Python SDK merges retry attempts to reduce load (retry-coalescing). When a retry is retried by the orchestrator and the SDK coalesces retries, downstream webhook receives two nearly-identical POSTs: same payload, same idempotency token header, but different TCP connection metadata. Downstream reports two successful completions and triggers side effects.

Expected behavior: SDK should ensure at-most-once semantics for tool/function calls where an idempotency token exists, or clearly document that coalescing can only be used when downstream supports dedup by payload fingerprint.

Notes: Customer provided code snippets, logs, and an attachable minimal repro. They are concerned that coalescing + background credential refresh creates a race where both the original inflight and the coalesced retry surface to the serving runtime as separate executions.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy a Python worker (python-sdk v1.17.1) configured with retry_coalesce=true and idempotency_token header set per-request.
2) Start a long-running function/tool call that triggers an external webhook from inside the function.
3) During execution, restart the worker process (simulate rolling deploy).
4) Trigger client-side retry by initiating a network reconnect from the TS orchestrator.
5) Observe downstream webhook logs for duplicate POSTs with identical idempotency token but different connection ids.

(Customer provided a compact repro repo Gist: https://gist.github.com/brightcart/retry-coalesce-repro)

2026-03-11 11:05 - Priya Shah (Runtime Eng): Initial hypothesis: idempotency token normalization differs between SDK and runtime (whitespace/charset trimming). If coalescing alters canonicalization, runtime dedupe hash mismatches and both executions proceed. Asking for raw headers captured from both dispatch events.

Found a case where SDK applied URL-safe base64 and runtime expected strict base64 without padding. That changed the dedupe key. investigation_notes:
Hypotheses: 1) Coalescing in SDK merges higher-layer logical attempts but does not coordinate canonicalization with runtime; mismatch allows two executions. 2) Process restart causes in-flight state duplication: coordinator issues a fallback dispatch before it receives the coalesced cancellation ack.
Actions taken: - Reproduced with customer's gist on a local dedicated-like cluster. - Added boundary logs in runtime and SDK to capture canonicalized idempotency tokens. - Confirmed encoding mismatch: SDK produced base64url no-padding, runtime expected padded base64. - Check: also saw coalescing pick the older envelope which lacked Request-Nonce header, causing runtime to treat them as different lineage.
Relevant artifacts: runtime PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5217, internal runbook note INT-1510, dashboard link to runtime dispatch rates: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/runtime/dispatch?var-node=us-east
resolution:
Workaround provided: BrightCart temporarily disabled retry_coalesce=true on Python SDK (config flag) and enabled client-side dedupe by computing a request-level fingerprint (sha256 of payload) and sending as X-Client-Fingerprint header. This prevented duplicate downstream side effects.
Permanent fix: Engineering will land normalization in runtime (accept both base64url and base64 padded) and update the SDK to emit a canonical padded base64 idempotency token and ensure Request-Nonce is preserved across coalescing. ETA: patch merged and staged in canary (v1.17.4-rc) on 2026-03-15; full release scheduled v1.18.0 next week with coordinated runtime rollout.
Follow-ups: - Postmortem to include guidance on when retry_coalesce is safe to enable for customers with external side effects. - Add a note in SDK docs about canonical idempotency token format and suggested X-Client-Fingerprint fallback. - Add an integration test for coalescing + process restart in CI (ticket INT-1522).
next_steps: 1) Monitor canary after PR 5217 merge for duplicate dispatches (SRE). 2) Coordinate BrightCart patching plan: apply SDK update to v1.17.4-rc in a staging rollout (Support/SE). 3) Update docs and runbook (Docs + Developer Experience).
